Subject: Data-plane guardrails & isolation expectations — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call)

Thanks again for taking time today, Sylvia — good conversation. Quick written recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment on your isolation questions before the technical deep-dive.

Call recap (high level)
- Use-case: MedSync will run PHI-enriched clinical summarization and search for care teams; low tolerance for cross-tenant data exposure.
- Primary concern: explicit data-plane separation and custody of customer data + ability to demonstrate no co-mingling.
- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated or Private VPC, but team wants clarity on operational differences and proof points before committing.

Key distinctions we discussed (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live; multi-tenant controls, strict RBAC, but shared inference pools — not recommended if you require physical separation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your tenant; data-plane (inference input/output) and KV-cache are isolated to your capacity; control plane still runs in Redwood's managed control plane unless Private is chosen.
- Private VPC/on-prem: full customer-managed network and optional on-prem package; control plane can be private; suitable when you need both data sovereignty and control-plane residency.

Attachments: I attached our latest privacy matrix & a short questionnaire you mentioned during the call.
[Attachment: redwood-privacy-matrix-v2.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]
[Attachment: medsync-deployment-questions.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

Suggested immediate next steps
1) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (network & KMS) — please share availability for next week.
2) We’ll prepare a short two-slide summary that maps MedSync's top requirements to Dedicated vs Private VPC (ops, latency, cost, auditability).
3) If helpful, we can provision a short Dedicated-capacity perf artifact to show tenant-only inference with a sanitized prompt set.

Ask: can you confirm whether your procurement/legal team requires control-plane separation (BYOK + private control plane) or if control-plane residency in Redwood with strict audit logs would be acceptable as a step one?

Thanks,

Aditya — thank you for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement asks that any PHI processed by a vendor be logically segregated and that evidence of no cross-customer leakage be demonstrable. Physical separation (dedicated GPUs) is preferred but not strictly mandatory if you can show strong KV/prefix isolation + auditable traces.
2) Security is likely to request BYOK for keys used in model encryption and audit logs that show token-level access traces for at least 13 months.
3) Control plane: initial preference is to keep the control plane managed if we can get the BYOK and detailed audit logs; we may escalate to private control plane if the security team still flags residual risk.

Also, Marissa asked if you can confirm whether Redwood supports a short evidence package (e.g., tenancy/topology diagram, KV cache eviction behavior, and a short timeline for audit log retention) — that would help our internal risk review.

I'm available for the tech deep-dive Tue/Wed next week morning PT.

Sylvia Kim
Head of Cloud & Security, MedSync Health

Sylvia — adding a bit of technical clarity from an ops/security POV (so your reviewers have concrete language):

Short answers to your asks:
- Tenancy/topology diagram: yes — I attached a tenant topology diagram and a short note on KV cache isolation semantics.
- KV cache eviction & data lifecycle: inference KV/cache entries are scoped to model sessions and stored only on the tenant’s dedicated capacity (for Dedicated) or inside the VPC-hosted instances (for Private). We can configure TTLs and explicit flush on cutover.
- Audit logs & retention: Redwood supports token-level request logs, model/version identifiers, and can retain audit logs for 13+ months as part of an enterprise retention add-on; we can produce sample log slices for review.

Where Dedicated vs Private differs materially (ops language)
- Dedicated capacity: provides GPU and runtime isolation for inference. Control plane (deployment management, billing) remains in Redwood's managed plane. Good fit if you want strong data-plane separation with relatively faster provisioning and lower TCO than full Private.
- Private VPC/on-prem: gives you network residency, private control plane option, and direct KMS/HSM integration under your tenancy. Higher operational lift but aligns with customers requiring strict control-plane separation or regulatory constraints.

Proposed next steps (ops):
1) We’ll send the tenancy diagram + a one-page KV/cache semantics note (attached).
2) Aditya to schedule tech deep-dive with our infra engineer (Karthik) and your security lead — 60 minutes.
3) Post deep-dive: we can produce an evidence pack (diagram + sample log extract + template SOC/Security artifact) under NDA if needed.
